Name: add
Description: Adds {rs} and {rt} and places the sum in {rd}, trapping on signed overflow. IDO normally emits addu instead.

Name: addu
Description: Adds {rs} and {rt} and places the sum in {rd}. The 'u' means no overflow trap, not unsigned: this is the everyday 32-bit add for signed and unsigned values alike.

Name: addi
Description: Adds the sign-extended 16-bit immediate {imm} to {rs} and places the sum in {rt}, trapping on signed overflow. IDO normally emits addiu instead.

Name: addiu
Description: Adds the sign-extended 16-bit immediate {imm} to {rs} and places the sum in {rt}, with no overflow trap. With rs = zero it simply loads the constant {imm}; it also moves the stack pointer in the prologue and epilogue and adds the low half of an address after a lui.

Name: sub
Description: Subtracts {rt} from {rs} and places the difference in {rd}, trapping on signed overflow. IDO normally emits subu instead.

Name: subu
Description: Subtracts {rt} from {rs} and places the difference in {rd}, with no overflow trap. Used for signed and unsigned subtraction alike.

Name: negu
Description: Negates {rt} and places the result in {rd}. An alias for subu rd, zero, rt.

Name: mult
Description: Multiplies {rs} by {rt} as signed 32-bit values. The 64-bit product lands in the HI/LO register pair; mflo reads the low 32 bits (the C result) and mfhi the high 32.

Name: multu
Description: Multiplies {rs} by {rt} as unsigned 32-bit values. The 64-bit product lands in HI/LO; mflo reads the low 32 bits and mfhi the high 32. IDO also uses multu for signed multiplies when only the low word matters.

Name: div
Description: Divides {rs} by {rt} as signed 32-bit values. The quotient goes to LO (read with mflo) and the remainder to HI (read with mfhi), so the same instruction serves both / and %. IDO follows it with a break 7 guard against dividing by zero and a break 6 guard against overflow.

Name: divu
Description: Divides {rs} by {rt} as unsigned 32-bit values. The quotient goes to LO (mflo) and the remainder to HI (mfhi). IDO follows it with a break 7 guard against dividing by zero.

Name: mflo
Description: Copies the LO register into {rd}: the low 32 bits of the last multiply, or the quotient of the last divide.

Name: mfhi
Description: Copies the HI register into {rd}: the high 32 bits of the last multiply, or the remainder of the last divide.

Name: mtlo
Description: Copies {rs} into the LO register.

Name: mthi
Description: Copies {rs} into the HI register.

Name: daddu
Description: Adds the full 64-bit values in {rs} and {rt} and places the sum in {rd}, with no overflow trap.

Name: daddiu
Description: Adds the sign-extended 16-bit immediate {imm} to the full 64-bit value in {rs} and places the sum in {rt}.

Name: dsubu
Description: Subtracts the 64-bit value in {rt} from {rs} and places the difference in {rd}, with no overflow trap.

Name: dmult
Description: Multiplies {rs} by {rt} as signed 64-bit values. The 128-bit product lands in HI/LO.

Name: dmultu
Description: Multiplies {rs} by {rt} as unsigned 64-bit values. The 128-bit product lands in HI/LO.

Name: ddiv
Description: Divides {rs} by {rt} as signed 64-bit values. The quotient goes to LO and the remainder to HI.

Name: ddivu
Description: Divides {rs} by {rt} as unsigned 64-bit values. The quotient goes to LO and the remainder to HI.

Name: and
Description: Bitwise ANDs {rs} with {rt} and places the result in {rd}.

Name: andi
Description: Bitwise ANDs {rs} with the zero-extended 16-bit immediate {imm} and places the result in {rt}. Common for masking (& 0xff, & 0xffff) and for testing single bits; it also zero-extends a narrow value.

Name: or
Description: Bitwise ORs {rs} with {rt} and places the result in {rd}. With rt = zero this is a plain register copy, which is how IDO moves a value into another register; or rd, zero, zero sets {rd} to 0.

Name: ori
Description: Bitwise ORs {rs} with the zero-extended 16-bit immediate {imm} and places the result in {rt}. After a lui it fills in the low half of a 32-bit constant; with rs = zero it loads an unsigned 16-bit constant.

Name: xor
Description: Bitwise XORs {rs} with {rt} and places the result in {rd}.

Name: xori
Description: Bitwise XORs {rs} with the zero-extended 16-bit immediate {imm} and places the result in {rt}. xori with 1 flips a boolean; IDO also uses it to compare against a constant (the result is zero only on equality).

Name: nor
Description: Bitwise NORs {rs} with {rt} into {rd}: each bit is set only if it is clear in both. With rt = zero it is a bitwise NOT of {rs}.

Name: not
Description: Inverts every bit of {rs} and places the result in {rd}. An alias for nor rd, rs, zero.

Name: move
Description: Copies {rs} into {rd}. An alias for or rd, rs, zero (or addu rd, rs, zero).

Name: li
Description: Loads the constant {imm} into {rt}. An alias for addiu rt, zero, imm or ori rt, zero, imm.

Name: lui
Description: Places {imm} in the upper 16 bits of {rt} and zeroes the lower 16. The first half of building a 32-bit constant or the address of a global: an ori, addiu, or the offset of a following load/store supplies the low half.

Name: sll
Description: Shifts {rt} left by {sa} bits and places the result in {rd}, filling with zeros. A left shift by n multiplies by 2 to the n, which is how IDO scales an array index; sll by 24 or 16 followed by sra is how it sign-extends a byte or halfword.

Name: srl
Description: Shifts {rt} right by {sa} bits and places the result in {rd}, filling from the left with zeros: an unsigned divide by 2 to the {sa}.

Name: sra
Description: Shifts {rt} right by {sa} bits and places the result in {rd}, copying the sign bit into the vacated positions: a signed divide by 2 to the {sa}, rounding toward negative infinity. Also the second half of an sll/sra sign-extension pair.

Name: sllv
Description: Shifts {rt} left by the amount in the low 5 bits of {rs} and places the result in {rd}.

Name: srlv
Description: Shifts {rt} right by the amount in the low 5 bits of {rs}, filling with zeros, and places the result in {rd}.

Name: srav
Description: Shifts {rt} right by the amount in the low 5 bits of {rs}, copying the sign bit in, and places the result in {rd}.

Name: dsll
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} left by {sa} bits and places the result in {rd}.

Name: dsll32
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} left by {sa} + 32 bits and places the result in {rd}.

Name: dsrl
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} right by {sa} bits, filling with zeros, and places the result in {rd}.

Name: dsrl32
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} right by {sa} + 32 bits, filling with zeros, and places the result in {rd}.

Name: dsra
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} right by {sa} bits, copying the sign bit in, and places the result in {rd}.

Name: dsra32
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} right by {sa} + 32 bits, copying the sign bit in, and places the result in {rd}. dsra32 by 0 extracts the high word of a 64-bit value.

Name: dsllv
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} left by the amount in the low 6 bits of {rs} and places the result in {rd}.

Name: dsrlv
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} right by the amount in the low 6 bits of {rs}, filling with zeros, and places the result in {rd}.

Name: dsrav
Description: Shifts the 64-bit value in {rt} right by the amount in the low 6 bits of {rs}, copying the sign bit in, and places the result in {rd}.

Name: slt
Description: Sets {rd} to 1 if {rs} is less than {rt} as signed values, otherwise 0. Comparisons that are not a simple branch condition are built from this plus xori or a branch on the result.

Name: sltu
Description: Sets {rd} to 1 if {rs} is less than {rt} as unsigned values, otherwise 0. sltu rd, zero, rt tests whether {rt} is non-zero.

Name: slti
Description: Sets {rt} to 1 if {rs} is less than the sign-extended immediate {imm} as signed values, otherwise 0.

Name: sltiu
DescriptiveName: Set on Less Than Immediate Unsigned
Description: Sets {rt} to 1 if {rs} is less than the sign-extended immediate {imm} as unsigned values, otherwise 0. sltiu rt, rs, 1 tests whether {rs} is zero; sltiu against a small constant is how IDO range-checks a switch value.

Name: lb
Description: Loads the byte at {base} + {offset} into {rt}, sign-extending it to 32 bits: a signed char (s8).

Name: lbu
Description: Loads the byte at {base} + {offset} into {rt}, zero-extending it to 32 bits: an unsigned char (u8).

Name: lh
Description: Loads the 16-bit halfword at {base} + {offset} into {rt}, sign-extending it to 32 bits: a signed short (s16).

Name: lhu
Description: Loads the 16-bit halfword at {base} + {offset} into {rt}, zero-extending it to 32 bits: an unsigned short (u16).

Name: lw
Description: Loads the 32-bit word at {base} + {offset} into {rt}: an int, a pointer, or a saved register coming back off the stack.

Name: lwu
Description: Loads the 32-bit word at {base} + {offset} into {rt}, zero-extending it to 64 bits.

Name: ld
Description: Loads the 64-bit doubleword at {base} + {offset} into {rt}.

Name: lwl
Description: Loads the high-order bytes of an unaligned word starting at {base} + {offset} into the left part of {rt}. Paired with lwr; IDO emits the pair to copy or read packed struct data that is not 4-byte aligned.

Name: lwr
Description: Loads the low-order bytes of an unaligned word ending at {base} + {offset} into the right part of {rt}, completing an lwl.

Name: sb
Description: Stores the low byte of {rt} to {base} + {offset}: a write to a char / s8 / u8.

Name: sh
Description: Stores the low 16 bits of {rt} to {base} + {offset}: a write to a short / s16 / u16.

Name: sw
Description: Stores the 32-bit word in {rt} to {base} + {offset}: an int, a pointer, or a register being saved to the stack.

Name: sd
Description: Stores the 64-bit doubleword in {rt} to {base} + {offset}.

Name: swl
Description: Stores the high-order bytes of {rt} to an unaligned word starting at {base} + {offset}. Paired with swr for unaligned or packed struct writes.

Name: swr
Description: Stores the low-order bytes of {rt} to an unaligned word ending at {base} + {offset}, completing an swl.

Name: beq
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} equals {rt}. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bne
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} does not equal {rt}. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: beqz
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is zero. An alias for beq rs, zero, target; a test for 0, NULL, or false. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bnez
DescriptiveName: Branch on Not Equal to Zero
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is not zero. An alias for bne rs, zero, target. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: b
Description: Branches unconditionally to {target}. An alias for beq zero, zero, target. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: blez
DescriptiveName: Branch on Less Than or Equal to Zero
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is less than or equal to zero (signed). The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bgtz
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is greater than zero (signed). The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bltz
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is negative (its sign bit is set). The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bgez
DescriptiveName: Branch on Greater Than or Equal to Zero
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is zero or positive (its sign bit is clear). The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bltzal
DescriptiveName: Branch on Less Than Zero and Link
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is negative, saving the return address in ra. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bgezal
DescriptiveName: Branch on Greater Than or Equal to Zero and Link
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is zero or positive, saving the return address in ra. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bal
Description: Branches unconditionally to {target} and saves the return address in ra: a PC-relative call. An alias for bgezal zero, target. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: beql
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} equals {rt}. Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bnel
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} does not equal {rt}. Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: beqzl
DescriptiveName: Branch on Equal to Zero Likely
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is zero (an alias for beql rs, zero, target). Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bnezl
DescriptiveName: Branch on Not Equal to Zero Likely
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is not zero (an alias for bnel rs, zero, target). Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: blezl
DescriptiveName: Branch on Less Than or Equal to Zero Likely
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is less than or equal to zero (signed). Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bgtzl
DescriptiveName: Branch on Greater Than Zero Likely
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is greater than zero (signed). Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bltzl
DescriptiveName: Branch on Less Than Zero Likely
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is negative. Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bgezl
DescriptiveName: Branch on Greater Than or Equal to Zero Likely
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is zero or positive. Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bltzall
DescriptiveName: Branch on Less Than Zero and Link Likely
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is negative, saving the return address in ra. Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bgezall
DescriptiveName: Branch on Greater Than or Equal to Zero and Link Likely
Description: Branches to {target} if {rs} is zero or positive, saving the return address in ra. Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bc1t
Description: Branches to {target} if the FPU condition flag is set by the most recent c.xx.s / c.xx.d compare. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bc1f
Description: Branches to {target} if the FPU condition flag is clear after the most recent c.xx.s / c.xx.d compare. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: bc1tl
Description: Branches to {target} if the FPU condition flag is set by the most recent c.xx.s / c.xx.d compare. Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: bc1fl
Description: Branches to {target} if the FPU condition flag is clear after the most recent c.xx.s / c.xx.d compare. Branch-likely form: the delay slot instruction executes only when the branch is taken and is skipped otherwise, so IDO uses these for loop back-edges and puts the next iteration's first instruction in the slot.

Name: j
Description: Jumps unconditionally to {target}. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: jal
Description: Calls the function at {target}: saves the return address in ra and jumps. The delay slot instruction executes first, so IDO often sets up the last argument there.

Name: jr
Description: Jumps to the address in {rs}. jr ra returns from the function; a jr through another register is usually a switch jump table. The delay slot instruction executes first, which is why the return value or a final store often sits right after jr ra.

Name: jalr
Description: Calls the function whose address is in {rs}, saving the return address in ra: a call through a function pointer. The instruction in the delay slot below always executes before the branch takes effect.

Name: nop
Description: Does nothing. Fills a branch or jump delay slot when the compiler has nothing useful to put there, or pads the schedule between dependent instructions.

Name: break
Description: Raises a breakpoint exception with code {code}. IDO emits break 7 right after a div or divu to trap division by zero, and break 6 in its signed-overflow check for dividing INT_MIN by -1.

Name: syscall
Description: Raises a system call exception to the kernel.

Name: sync
Description: Waits for all earlier loads and stores to complete before any later ones begin.

Name: cache
Description: Performs cache operation {op} on the line containing {base} + {offset}. Only seen in OS and driver code.

Name: mfc0
Description: Copies system control register {rd} into {rt}. Only seen in OS and exception code.

Name: mtc0
Description: Copies {rt} into system control register {rd}. Only seen in OS and exception code.

Name: lwc1
Description: Loads the 32-bit float at {base} + {offset} into FPU register {ft}.

Name: swc1
Description: Stores the single-precision float in FPU register {ft} to {base} + {offset}.

Name: ldc1
Description: Loads the 64-bit double at {base} + {offset} into FPU register {ft}.

Name: sdc1
Description: Stores the double in FPU register {ft} to {base} + {offset}.

Name: mtc1
Description: Copies the raw 32 bits of {rt} into FPU register {fs} with no conversion. This is how an int reaches the FPU ahead of a cvt.s.w, and how a float constant assembled in an integer register gets there; mtc1 zero, fs loads 0.0f.

Name: mfc1
Description: Copies the raw 32 bits of FPU register {fs} into {rt} with no conversion. This is how the integer produced by trunc.w.s reaches a general register.

Name: dmtc1
Description: Copies the full 64 bits of {rt} into FPU register {fs} with no conversion.

Name: dmfc1
Description: Copies the full 64 bits of FPU register {fs} into {rt} with no conversion.

Name: ctc1
Description: Writes {rt} into FPU control register {fs}, usually to change the rounding mode.

Name: cfc1
Description: Reads FPU control register {fs} into {rt}.

Name: add.s
Description: Adds the single-precision floats {fs} and {ft} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: sub.s
Description: Subtracts the single-precision float {ft} from {fs} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: mul.s
Description: Multiplies the single-precision floats {fs} and {ft} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: div.s
Description: Divides the single-precision float {fs} by {ft} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: abs.s
Description: Places the absolute value of the single-precision float {fs} in {fd}.

Name: neg.s
Description: Negates the single-precision float {fs} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: mov.s
Description: Copies the single-precision float {fs} into {fd}.

Name: sqrt.s
Description: Places the square root of the single-precision float {fs} in {fd}.

Name: trunc.w.s
Description: Converts the float (f32) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd}, rounding toward zero: the C (s32) cast of a float (f32). An mfc1 usually follows to move the result to an integer register.

Name: trunc.l.s
Description: Converts the float (f32) in {fs} to a 64-bit integer in {fd}, rounding toward zero.

Name: round.w.s
Description: Converts the float (f32) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd}, rounding to nearest.

Name: ceil.w.s
Description: Converts the float (f32) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd}, rounding up.

Name: floor.w.s
Description: Converts the float (f32) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd}, rounding down.

Name: cvt.w.s
Description: Converts the float (f32) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd} using the current rounding mode. IDO prefers trunc.w.s for C casts.

Name: cvt.l.s
Description: Converts the float (f32) in {fs} to a 64-bit integer in {fd} using the current rounding mode.

Name: c.eq.s
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} equals {ft} as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag. A != compare uses the same instruction with the branch sense inverted.

Name: c.lt.s
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than {ft} as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag. IDO compiles a > b as c.lt with the operands swapped.

Name: c.le.s
DescriptiveName: Compare Less Than or Equal Single
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than or equal to {ft} as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag. IDO compiles a >= b as c.le with the operands swapped.

Name: c.un.s
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if either {fs} or {ft} is NaN as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ueq.s
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} equals {ft} or either is NaN as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ult.s
DescriptiveName: Compare Unordered or Less Than Single
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than {ft} or either is NaN as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ule.s
DescriptiveName: Compare Unordered or Less Than or Equal Single
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than or equal to {ft} or either is NaN as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.olt.s
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than {ft} and neither is NaN as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ole.s
DescriptiveName: Compare Ordered Less Than or Equal Single
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than or equal to {ft} and neither is NaN as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.nge.s
DescriptiveName: Compare Not Greater Than or Equal Single
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is not greater than or equal to {ft} (true for NaN) as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ngt.s
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is not greater than {ft} (true for NaN) as single-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: add.d
Description: Adds the double-precision floats {fs} and {ft} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: sub.d
Description: Subtracts the double-precision float {ft} from {fs} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: mul.d
Description: Multiplies the double-precision floats {fs} and {ft} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: div.d
Description: Divides the double-precision float {fs} by {ft} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: abs.d
Description: Places the absolute value of the double-precision float {fs} in {fd}.

Name: neg.d
Description: Negates the double-precision float {fs} and places the result in {fd}.

Name: mov.d
Description: Copies the double-precision float {fs} into {fd}.

Name: sqrt.d
Description: Places the square root of the double-precision float {fs} in {fd}.

Name: trunc.w.d
Description: Converts the double (f64) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd}, rounding toward zero: the C (s32) cast of a double (f64). An mfc1 usually follows to move the result to an integer register.

Name: trunc.l.d
Description: Converts the double (f64) in {fs} to a 64-bit integer in {fd}, rounding toward zero.

Name: round.w.d
Description: Converts the double (f64) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd}, rounding to nearest.

Name: ceil.w.d
Description: Converts the double (f64) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd}, rounding up.

Name: floor.w.d
Description: Converts the double (f64) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd}, rounding down.

Name: cvt.w.d
Description: Converts the double (f64) in {fs} to a 32-bit integer in {fd} using the current rounding mode. IDO prefers trunc.w.d for C casts.

Name: cvt.l.d
Description: Converts the double (f64) in {fs} to a 64-bit integer in {fd} using the current rounding mode.

Name: c.eq.d
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} equals {ft} as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag. A != compare uses the same instruction with the branch sense inverted.

Name: c.lt.d
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than {ft} as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag. IDO compiles a > b as c.lt with the operands swapped.

Name: c.le.d
DescriptiveName: Compare Less Than or Equal Double
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than or equal to {ft} as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag. IDO compiles a >= b as c.le with the operands swapped.

Name: c.un.d
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if either {fs} or {ft} is NaN as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ueq.d
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} equals {ft} or either is NaN as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ult.d
DescriptiveName: Compare Unordered or Less Than Double
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than {ft} or either is NaN as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ule.d
DescriptiveName: Compare Unordered or Less Than or Equal Double
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than or equal to {ft} or either is NaN as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.olt.d
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than {ft} and neither is NaN as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ole.d
DescriptiveName: Compare Ordered Less Than or Equal Double
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is less than or equal to {ft} and neither is NaN as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.nge.d
DescriptiveName: Compare Not Greater Than or Equal Double
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is not greater than or equal to {ft} (true for NaN) as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: c.ngt.d
Description: Sets the FPU condition flag if {fs} is not greater than {ft} (true for NaN) as double-precision floats, and clears it otherwise. A following bc1t or bc1f branches on the flag.

Name: cvt.s.w
Description: Converts the 32-bit integer in {fs} to a single-precision float in {fd}: the (f32) cast of an int, after an mtc1 moved the integer into the FPU.

Name: cvt.d.w
Description: Converts the 32-bit integer in {fs} to a double in {fd}: the (f64) cast of an int, after an mtc1 moved the integer into the FPU.

Name: cvt.s.l
Description: Converts the 64-bit integer in {fs} to a single-precision float in {fd}.

Name: cvt.d.l
Description: Converts the 64-bit integer in {fs} to a double in {fd}.

Name: cvt.s.d
Description: Converts the double in {fs} to a single-precision float in {fd}: the (f32) cast of a double, or the narrowing back after arithmetic was promoted to double.

Name: cvt.d.s
Description: Converts the single-precision float in {fs} to a double in {fd}: the promotion that happens when a float meets a double, a double constant, or an unprototyped function argument.
